focus: CLI surface and output: list, describe, health and tool commands, stdout structuredContent, preview files, startup cost, persistent probe cache, shared MEDIA_EDITOR_DATA_DIR
keyQuestions: What CLI command surface, JSON output contract, preview handling, startup cost, and shared data folder satisfy direct terminal use?
answeredQuestions: What CLI command surface, JSON output contract, preview handling, startup cost, and shared data folder satisfy direct terminal use?

label: The command surface landed as list, describe, health and tool commands (cli.ts:413-451), and running the built CLI confirmed exactly 40 tools with media_health first, while describe image_convert printed the placement fields fileName, subfolder, targetFolder plus maxBytes in the listed schema.

list prints name, title and description for all entries of ALL_TOOLS (cli.ts:322-330, 60-62) and describe adds annotations plus z.toJSONSchema of the listed schema (cli.ts:332-340), needing no schema dependency beyond the existing zod ^4.6.5 (package.json:30).

One JSON argument source per call: --args, --args-file, or stdin when not a TTY (cli.ts:248-278), with mutual exclusion at 170-172 and non-object payloads rejected at 274-277. Individual tool flags are deliberately not accepted.

stdout receives exactly the structuredContent object (cli.ts:388), diagnostics go to stderr (cli.ts:192-194, 206-214), and exit codes distinguish tool failure 1 from usage or dispatch error 2 and startup failure 3 (cli.ts:389, 203, 460).

The preview lands as a file: PreviewSink is a CLI-only context dependency (tool-context.ts:112, 126), withPreviewBlock returns previewPath in structuredContent instead of the base64 block (preview.ts:118-137), and the sink writes dataDir/previews/preview-uuid.jpg atomically through a registered temp file (cli.ts:280-305) while MCP keeps the inline image block.

Startup cost measured warm on this machine: baseline 0.02s, sharp import 0.06s, all-tools import 0.13s, and node dist/cli.js list end to end 0.11s printing 16317 bytes, which resolves the schema-manifest question toward keeping the eager import at roughly a tenth of a second per call.

The persistent cache landed as dataDir/cache/probes.json (probe-cache.ts:53, 183-197), storing binary resolutions and encoder and filter lists keyed by absolute path, size, mtime and version (probe-cache.ts:21-41), and the CLI constructs it per call from config.dataDir (cli.ts:381).

One shared data folder is preserved end to end: MEDIA_EDITOR_DATA_DIR (config.ts:92) is fed by --data-dir (cli.ts:239-241), setup installs under dataDir/bin (setup-ffmpeg.ts:252, 441), health reports dataFolder (health.ts:204), and cache and previews read the same folder, so media_setup_ffmpeg then media_health work across separate CLI calls.

Two carried-forward observations: the parse at dispatch.ts:116 is a plain z.object safeParse so a mistyped JSON key is stripped silently with no warning, and CLI tests are in flight untracked beside the implementation (tests/cli/cli-process.vitest.ts 19 cases, tests/cli/dispatch.vitest.ts 7, tests/core/probe-cache.vitest.ts 7).
